newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman petchem plant seen on stream 2001-2002 - BP.
newsitem.headline: Oman petchem plant seen on stream 2001-2002 - BP.

text.p: A planned $900 million petrochemical plant in the Gulf Arab state of Oman is scheduled to come on stream between 2001 and 2002, a British Petroleum Co Plc spokesman said on Monday.
Oman on Sunday named BP Chemicals as its foreign partner in a project to build a petrochemical plant capable of producing 450,000 tonnes a year of ethylene and polyethylene.
"2001-2002 is the kind of time frame we are looking at," said a BP spokesman in London.

It would be the sultanate's first major venture into the petrochemical sector which will exploit the country's gas deposits which are being mainly developed to supply a $6 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project.
A BP-Omani study is underway to evaluate the economics of and equity participants in the project, the spokesman said.
BP will take a 40-49 percent stake in the project, 40 percent would be open for public subscription and the rest will go to the state-owned Oman Oil Company, Gulf papers said on Monday.
The proposed project would need to be approved by BP's board of directors before going ahead, the BP spokesman said.
Ethylene is one of the major building blocks of the chemical industries, its main derivative being polyethylene which is widely used to make plastics.
The plant at Sohar, 200 km (125 miles) north of Muscat would be primarily geared towards the export market.
Oman is also developing its gas reserves to supply a proposed fertiliser and aluminium plant in addition to the LNG project.
